highlights.text: Play on a duel opens its room again
Every pip in a duel wears its own look
Your pips on Home wear your look
The Wardrobe opens while you're offline
All items shows the looks you can earn
Pollen rows show what each bonus added

paragraphs.text: Play on a duel opens the duel's room again. Whichever of you taps Play first makes the room, and your partner joins it, whoever's turn it is. If the room can't open, the game comes back to the duel page and says why. Every pip on the duel pages wears its player's look, your pip sits in your own seat whether you started the pair or joined it, and the other pair's run plays each turn in the looks they wore. Start a duel shows each friend in the look they last wore. Duel pages scroll with your finger, long names stay readable, the lobby tiles fit on a phone and Leave duel stays on screen.

When your phone is offline, the buttons that need the internet grey out, like Play with your friend, Duels and Add friend. Tap one and the game tells you it needs a connection. They come back by themselves once you're online. If you've opened the Wardrobe before, it opens offline too. You can put things on and take them off, and friends see your new look once you're back online. Buy stays greyed until then.

All items in the Wardrobe lists the looks you earn by playing, the Gold leaf, Every Hard and the Top 10 ribbon, even before you have them. Pick one to try it on your pip and see how to earn it. They're never for sale. After a turn, each Pollen bonus row shows its percent and the Pollen it added, like First try (25%), and the rows above This turn add up to it.

Both pips on Home wear your look, as they do in a solo chapter. The Daisy is half again as big. The Lantern sits on the side of the head away from the leaf, and the views of your pip pull back so it stays in frame. The Tide's lower shade is deeper.

While your time waits for its check, a card beside the leaderboard says so. You and your partner see its place right away, and other players see it once the check passes. In What's new, tapping an earlier version opens it where it is, and the list no longer jumps to the end.

Showing or copying your recovery code asks for your screen lock first, if your phone has one, and the code stays out of screenshots and the recent apps picture. When you pick a name, Use my Play Games name shows straight away, and tapping it signs you in to Play Games if you aren't already.

The Full Journey row after a turn shows how many of you have it and the Pollen it added, like Full Journey (2 × 10%). Your first monthly Pollen from Full Journey arrives right after you subscribe, and months paid while you were away share one card with their total. On Home, your pip walks round the low dip of the Rolling Rail.

highlights.text: Tap your Pollen balance to open the Pollen page
Short of Pollen? Buy the bundle you need on the spot
Your leaderboard place shows as soon as you finish
Friends see each other's looks
Duels update as they happen
More room to walk in Explore
The Lighthouse stays lit until you rest the lamp

paragraphs.text: Tapping your Pollen balance on Home or in the Wardrobe opens the Pollen page, which used to be called Pollen from play. The Wardrobe button and your balance show up on Home every time, including right after the game starts and when you come back from a solo chapter. Friends see each other's looks too. A friend's pip used to show up plain when they wore something your phone hadn't seen yet. A look you put on after your last turn in a room reaches your friend after your next turn there.

Pollen prices in the Wardrobe and on a name change no longer have a rough dollar amount beside them. On the Owned tab of the Wardrobe, Hat, Body and Leaf each end with a Get more card that opens All items, as long as the shop has something you don't own yet.

Your Pollen balance has a + beside it, on Home too, and the + opens the Pollen store. Previous purchases, at the bottom of the store, holds your bundle receipts, which used to be in Settings. When an item or a name change costs more Pollen than you have, the Not enough Pollen yet card names the smallest bundle that covers the rest, or the one that gets you closest, and shows how much Pollen it gives. Its button shows the price and buys the bundle right there. Once the Pollen arrives, the item's card opens again, so you still choose whether to spend it.

When you finish a chapter together and your time makes the top 10, the end of the chapter celebrates your place at once instead of saying the time is being checked. On the leaderboard and under Your best, the run stands at its place with a small clock beside it until the check is done. It shows your pair's names if the board already lists them, and a first place shows the Gold leaf on your phone. A run that fails the check leaves the board.

Duels update as they happen. A challenge, an answer, a turn or a pair leaving shows in Open duels, on the duel page and in Party straight away while you're online, and within a minute otherwise. Results show as soon as both pairs finish. If you challenge a pair you already have a duel with on that chapter, the game opens that duel.

Explore has more room to walk. The keepsakes on Home stand further apart, three isles are wider and the Relay Masts face the other way. Your pip slides along whatever it walks into instead of stopping. The other pip keeps wandering while you explore, and both walk about again when you come back. Climb the steps and Turn the tide work from any side: your pip hops round the Giant Steps or the Tide Pool to where it starts. On the Relay Masts, the flag runs up its own cord, along the top line and back the same way.

Walk up to the Little House and its door swings open for your pip, which can't walk through it while it's shut. Ride the rail works from any side of the Rolling Rail, and your pip keeps its happy face until it lands. The Glasshouse flower stays grown until you push the pump again. After you wake the lamp, the Lighthouse beam keeps turning slowly until you press Rest the lamp.

highlights.text: Race another pair of friends in Duels
Race Our run or a top time from the leaderboard
100 Pollen the first time you beat Our run on a chapter
A bell rings when your pair wins
Online rooms open without a pause

paragraphs.text: Duels are on Home, under Friends. You play every duel as a pair, so open Party first and ask a friend to be your duel partner. Then tap Start a duel, pick a friend's pair and a chapter you both have open, and send the challenge. Challenges from your friends show under Open duels, where you can accept them. Each pair plays the chapter in its own room, taking turns as usual, and the faster pair wins. Only time spent playing counts, so waiting for a turn adds nothing. Your pair can have 3 duels going at once.

Turns in a friend duel earn extra Pollen. The duel result and the Pollen card after each turn list it as the duel bonus, with its percent. Both players in the winning pair also get a win bonus, for up to 3 wins a week and one a week against the same pair. After a friend duel, Watch their run plays the other pair's run.

Race a recorded run, under Open duels, lets your pair race a time on any chapter you have open. Pick Our run, the time we set ourselves, or one of the top times on the chapter's leaderboard. A race pays Pollen like any turn together, and you each get 100 Pollen the first time you beat Our run on a chapter.

When your pair wins a duel or beats a recorded run, the first place bell from the leaderboards rings the first time you open the result. Duels always play with Forgiving catches off, and duel runs share the chapter's leaderboard with normal runs.
In a party, each Full Journey member adds 10% Pollen for both of you.
Opening an online room no longer freezes the screen for a moment. The room's world builds behind its loading card, the way a solo chapter does.

highlights.text: Your pip hops up the Giant Steps and slides down happy
New water sounds in chapters and on Home
Sounds for the Wardrobe, Pollen and leaderboards
A soft tick on every button
Better layouts on tablets and folding phones

paragraphs.text: In Explore, walk your pip up to the front of the Giant Steps and it hops up them one step at a time, then sits at the top and slides down the chute with a happy face. Gold sparkles trail behind it, a heart pops up near the bottom, and your phone gives a light tap as it lands if Haptics is on. A tap on the Giant Steps still sends a ball the same way.

Drops fall down the shaft in the Wishing Well, and small waves wash up the shore in Turn of the Tide. The water goes quiet while a chapter or a replay is paused. On Home, the Wishing Well and Tide Pool keepsakes drip and splash as they play.
The Sleeping Lighthouse has the same waves on its shore, and buying something plays a sound when it goes through.

Putting something on or taking it off in the Wardrobe has its own sound, and so do Pollen arriving and reaching the top 10 on a leaderboard. Other buttons give a soft tick when you press them, except the ones you play a turn with, which already make their own sounds.

On tablets and folding phones, the Wardrobe and Pollen from play sit in the middle of the screen at a phone's height, the way Friends and Settings already do, so their cards no longer stretch to the top and bottom.

paragraphs.text: The shop in the Wardrobe opens. Spend the Pollen you earn by playing, or from a bundle, on hats, bodies, leaves and the two packs of reaction faces. Everything stays in the shop, so you can come back for it later.

The Pollen store is open. Tap the + beside your balance in the Wardrobe to see four bundles: Pinch, Pouch, Jar and Basket. Each card shows the price Google Play charges and how much Pollen you get for each dollar. Your first bundle adds 20% more Pollen, once. The receipts stay in Settings, under Account & recovery, in Pollen and purchases.
paragraphs.ios_text: The Pollen store is open on iPhone too. Tap the + beside your balance in the Wardrobe to see four bundles: Pinch, Pouch, Jar and Basket. Each card shows the App Store price and how much Pollen you get for each dollar. Your first bundle adds 20% more Pollen, once, whichever phone you buy it on. The receipts stay in Settings, under Account & recovery, in Pollen and purchases.

paragraphs.text: Full Journey comes to iPhone too, so a friend on an iPhone can host the paid chapters for you.
paragraphs.ios_text: Full Journey comes to iPhone as a subscription, by the month or by the year, with the App Store price shown before you pay. It opens the paid chapters and lets you host them for a friend. Restore purchases brings it back on a new phone, and Manage subscription opens your App Store subscriptions.

Some of them stand on three new isles: a tide isle and two isles behind Home. Tapping a keepsake still plays it.

paragraphs.text: The Pollen a turn earns now shows on one line, once, for both of you, and on the end card too, including after a Hard run. When you accept a friend request, their name shows straight away.

After a run together, the end card says where your time stands on the leaderboard: being checked, its place, or why it can't count. If Forgiving catches was on, the card has a button to turn it off. Home tells you while a time is being checked, and times are checked more often, so a place shows sooner. Under Your best, the board says why a time has no place, and its note explains which times can rank.
Forgiving catches is now off on every phone, so your times can count. You can turn it back on in Settings, and a note first tells you that leaderboard times won't count while it's on.

highlights.text: Chapters open one by one as you finish them
One keepsake for each chapter on Home, with upgrades
Fastest pair leaderboards for every chapter

Wear the looks you earn from the Wardrobe

paragraphs.text: Chapters now open in the order of the Chapters page. First Steps is open from the start, and finishing a chapter opens the next one, whether you finish it solo, with a friend or on Hard. A chapter you've already played, or have a room in, stays open, and finishing one further along opens every chapter before it. A locked card says which chapter to finish first. The earlier islands are always open.

Home has new keepsakes, one for each chapter, standing on the two islands. Clear a chapter solo or with a friend to earn its keepsake. It gains a new piece when you also clear the chapter with a friend, on Hard, and on Hard with a friend. The earlier islands share the Lantern Line, with a lantern for each island you clear. Tap a keepsake you've earned and it moves: the Bell Lift rings its bell and the Relay Flag goes up. The card under the islands says what each keepsake still needs and counts your keepsakes, upgrades and Hard clears. While you play a chapter, its keepsake stands in a corner of the island. If you sign in to Play Games, your Hard marks go into your cloud save too.

Tap a keepsake you've earned and it moves: the Bell Lift rings its bell and the Relay Flag goes up. The card under the islands says what each keepsake still needs and counts your keepsakes, upgrades and Hard clears. While you play a chapter, its keepsake stands in a corner of the island.

paragraphs.text: Friends has Leaderboards now. Each chapter has a Fastest pair board with the top 10 runs played together, and your own best sits under it. Tap Watch to see a top 10 run, with both turns played back as they were recorded. A new run is checked before it ranks, and the board shows its time while that happens. When your run makes the top 10, a short celebration shows on the board or on Home, with a bigger one for 3rd, 2nd and 1st. Pairs show as A pair unless both players turn on Show my name on leaderboards in Settings. Solo runs and runs with Forgiving catches on don't count. Report flags a time that looks wrong.

You earn Pollen now. A turn you play in a room with a friend pays Pollen, with more for a first try or a Hard turn, and the first time you clear a chapter pays extra. A full pay turn in a free chapter can bloom and pay double or triple, and Settings lists the odds under Lucky blooms. Each week a set number of turns pays in full, and after that a turn pays a little. The Wardrobe button at the top of Settings shows your Pollen and the looks you've earned: the Top 10 ribbon and the Gold leaf from the boards, and Every Hard for clearing every chapter on Hard with a friend. Your pip wears your look in your friends' rooms too.

The Sleeping Lighthouse has a normal card in Play Solo now, and Hard mode like every other chapter, solo or with a friend. It leads the Full Journey chapters in every chapter list, and finishing the last free chapter opens it. The other Full Journey chapters open one after another from there, and they still need Full Journey. If you get Full Journey before you reach the Lighthouse, After You says which chapter to finish first and has a button to your chapters.

In Turn of the Tide, the water wheels are valves now. Your pip stands on the valve's own spot to turn it, and each valve is the colour of the pip it belongs to. In Slack Water the chains are hand winches and the bars are sliding bolts, and the button says Pull chain or Pull bar. Valves, winches and bolts each have their own sound, and when a lot happens at once you still hear the water and your own control. Pads show as stand spots right where they count. Posts and catwalks that stay open under the high tide have walls so they stay dry, and the walls in front of your pip fade while it stands there. Turn of the Tide also gets ready while Home sits idle, so it opens faster.

Forgiving catches starts off on a new install, and an existing setting stays as it was. The filter for pip names and friend nicknames knows many more words. Watch all parts in Replays plays from the first part to the last, and you can remove a part from the wide preview. A Join, Host or New room you tap while a room loads now goes through. If a recovery saved on this phone can't finish, Settings lets you stop it. If a chapter's saved progress can't be read, it starts over and keeps the damaged copy on your phone. Android Back leaves the Earlier islands cards, and an update notice waits until you leave Explore.

It catches rude words split up with spaces or dots or spelled with numbers, and real words that only look close to one still pass. If Play Games sign in finishes after the name prompt opens, the prompt now offers your Play Games name.

highlights.text: Hard mode: play a whole chapter with no retries
A new Home, and the spirits are pips now
Chapters and screens open much faster
Rooms and Friends update almost at once
Give your pip a name, and add room partners as friends
Turn of the Tide is harder, and the water rises
See your tries and react when a run ends

paragraphs.text: Home has a new layout, with its menu in one panel on the left. Play with your friend has its own icon, two pips cheek to cheek with a heart, and when you hold the button they squeeze together and the heart pops. The spirits are called pips now. They have a new look too, with faces that change: they smile when they meet up or finish a chapter, and look sleepy while they doze. The birds on Home sing a few soft calls instead of one loud loop, and Explore lets you pinch to zoom. Empty lists of rooms, friends and replays have little drawings now.

Hard mode unlocks once you've finished a chapter, solo or with a friend. Pick Hard in Play Solo to play the whole chapter in one go, with no retries. One slip sends you back to stage 1, and the slip is kept in Replays under Hard runs so you can watch it. Each hard run you finish earns that chapter a Hard solo mark, and Home counts them beside your keepsakes. You can also host a hard room for a friend. One slip from either of you and you both go back to stage 1. Hard isn't available for the Sleeping Lighthouse. In normal play, a small pill shows which try you're on once you retry, and Replays shows how many tries a turn took. Replays shows your friend's tries for each turn too.

When a solo run ends, React on the card lets you pick a face or a heart, and it's kept with your replay. In a room, your reaction goes with your turn, and your friend's face shows on ending cards, room cards and Replays. Give your pip a name, or stay anonymous, and friends and room partners see it on rooms and replays. You can change it in Friends, and your invite page shows it. Sign in to Play Games in Settings to keep a copy of your progress in your account and bring your friend code to a new phone with one tap.

paragraphs.text: Turn of the Tide is harder now. A crossing no longer stays open just because you stepped onto it. Once nothing holds it open, the water rises over it, and a pip still on it drowns. In Slack Water the three posts stand in a row in front of the sea wheel, and the pin and the key have swapped steps. Doors and walls hold the water back wherever two levels meet, and stepping stones and lever pads stand in open water. A beacon marks where each turn ends, with an arrow at the edge of the screen when it's out of view. When you've done your part but a crossing still waits on the memory, a bubble says why. The winch says Raised or Lowered, and the slipway ramp swings down and up with it.

Chapters open much faster. While Home sits idle, After You gets the chapters' graphics ready, starting with the one you're likely to play next, so the first open after an install or an update stutters less. A chapter now appears in parts behind its opening card, and moving between screens no longer stalls while the old screen is cleared away. While you watch your own turn back, the pause card has Retry. If After You can't read your saved progress, it starts a new save, tells you once, and keeps the old file on your phone. On Android phones with a camera cutout, the picture fills the whole screen in landscape, and buttons and text stay clear of the cutout.

paragraphs.text: Settings is one page now, with its sections down the side. You can drag the pip at the top to spin it, and it squeezes its eyes shut while you hold it. Frame rate has three choices, 30, 60 or Unlimited, and 30 saves battery and keeps your phone cooler. Always skip waits skips the wait after you finish your turn, and a small mark shows while a wait is skipped or sped up. Low now draws as sharp as Balanced and still saves work by leaving out a few lights and effects. Low no longer draws shadows either, and the lighting stays as bright.

In a room, in your room list and in Friends, your friend's turns and requests now show up almost at once. Finished rooms have a menu where you can hide a room on this phone or leave it. Leaving deletes your photos and reactions in that room and takes it off your list, and your friend keeps the room and its replay. Hidden rooms wait in their own section with Show again. If you shared a room with someone who isn't your friend yet, Add friend sends them a request. Room options is sorted into Invite, Turns, Chapter and Safety, and while you wait in a room the camera moves in on the pips. Friend requests and messages pop up over any screen, with View to open Friends.

highlights.text: New sounds for water, the well and moving parts
Turn photos get a polaroid and survive the app closing
Chapters open faster
Spirits breathe and glance around while they wait

paragraphs.text: After You has new sounds. Footsteps sound on Home, with birds in the background, and bells have a real ring that other sounds don't cut short. A reel turns while the Wishing Well's bucket and ladder, the First Steps lift and the bridges move, and dropping down in the Wishing Well ends in a soft plunk. Turn of the Tide has lapping water and a rush as the water rises or falls. In the second turn, the memory's levers and switches make their sounds too.

When your spirit finishes before the memory does, it dozes by the goal while the camera follows the memory. A row under the chapter name shows who you're waiting for, and you can hold Fast-forward or tap Skip to end. A bell or beacon you reached first rings when the memory arrives. Resting spirits breathe now and glance around when they're alone, on the ready and waiting cards too. Speech bubbles on levers bob gently unless Reduce motion is on.

The optional turn photo has a new polaroid card, with the date written by hand along the bottom, like 15th Oct '26. If Android closed After You while the camera was open, you could land on Home with your turn saved and no photo. Now the photo is kept: Home says it's waiting, and Open room takes you back to send it with that turn.

Chapters open faster. They no longer wait for Home to finish checking your keepsakes, and every chapter builds behind the opening card straight to the stage you're on. Paid chapters open behind that one card too, without a checking card first. Enter the Lighthouse in the store now opens the six-stage Lighthouse, like its chapter card does.

Rooms cope better with quick taps. If the room hub is busy when you tap Continue, Open or Host, it shows Opening room and carries on. Begin and Resume stay live while a room refreshes, and a finished room's replay opens straight away. Your rooms loads faster, and a room that fails to load shows as unavailable instead of failing the whole list. Hosting or joining at the room limit now says so. Finished and closed rooms no longer count toward the 20 rooms you can have in play.
If Android backup is on, it now copies your solo progress and saved replays to your Google account, but only when the copy is encrypted with your phone's screen lock. Photos aren't included.

What's new is a button on Home, with a dot after an update, and See all changes opens the notes for every version on GitHub. Android Back now presses each screen's own way back and closes an open card first. Surfaces that flickered are fixed in several chapters, including the Wishing Well's rim and the Lighthouse's lens posts.

highlights.text: Easier on your phone, so it stays cooler
Taps in lists work the first time
Rooms with a friend recover when something fails
The spirit's shadow stops flickering

paragraphs.text: After You asks less of your phone now, to help it stay cooler. Play runs at up to 60 frames a second. Menus and cards draw at most 30 a second, and only when something changes, then go back to full speed as soon as you touch the screen. The 3D view is drawn at most 720 lines tall on Low and 1080 on Balanced. Once a chapter loads, its fixed scenery is folded into a few large pieces, so your phone draws far fewer of them every frame.
To play at your screen's full refresh rate, turn on Unlimited frame rate on the Graphics page. It uses more battery and can warm your phone.

Taps in lists work the first time, even if your finger moves a little while you press. Join on the Friends page stays live while the list refreshes, and a tap made during the refresh goes through once it lands.

Playing with a friend copes better when something goes wrong. A room your friend closed shows as closed in the room hub, and a turn sent to it moves into the room's history instead of holding up your other rooms. If the reply to a saved turn is lost, the game checks with the server and sends the turn again. A room the server refused for good no longer blocks the rest, and after a restart the hub reads the chapter list before it opens a room, so that room's turn can be saved. You also get a notification when your friend closes a room.
Play with a friend keeps the chapter you picked after you visit Friends or a room, so it doesn't fall back to First Steps anymore. Each room in the hub is named after its own chapter.
Watch replay opens the room you tapped it in, and saves a finished room's replay first if it needs to. Android Back now leaves Together replays the same way their Back button does.
